collection.title: Some open problems in quantum information theory

question.summary: Facet lists are complete only for small scenarios or restricted correlation spaces. No closed-form classification exists for arbitrary parties, settings and outcomes.
question.importance: Facet inequalities give the complete linear tests for classical locality in a fixed experiment. A general classification would organize Bell tests and identify which constraints can show quantum violations.
question.unresolved: Classify the facets of the local correlation polytope for general numbers of parties, settings and outcomes.

formulation.notation:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $N$ | Number of (spatially separated) subsystems on which measurements are performed |
| $M$ | Number of alternative observables measurable on each subsystem |
| $K$ | Number of possible outcomes per observable |
| $(N,M,K)$ | The triple specifying the correlation scenario |
| $(MK)^N$ | Total number of joint probabilities arising from $M^N$ experimental setups, each with $K^N$ outcomes |
| $K^{NM}$ | Number of deterministic local-hidden-variable extreme points (one value of $K$ assigned to each of the $NM$ observables) |
| $A_i, B_j$ | Dichotomic ($\pm 1$-valued) observables on the first/second subsystem (correlation-inequality form) |
| $\mathsf{E}(\cdot)$ | Expectation value of a product of dichotomic observables |
| $f$ | A candidate inequality vector (a face/Farkas vector) of the correlation polytope |
| $e_k$ | The $k$-th extreme point of the correlation polytope ($k=1,\ldots,R$) |
| CHSH | Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt inequality |
| GHZ | Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger state |
| PPT | Positive partial transpose |
| LOCC | Local operations and classical communication |
| $\rho$ | A bipartite (or multipartite) quantum state |
| $\rho^{T_A}$ | Partial transpose of $\rho$ over Alice's subsystem |

progress.title: Polyhedral sampling scales by giving up completeness
progress.detail: Staufenbiel's sampling method finds millions of classes in large scenarios but explicitly does not enumerate every facet.
progress.label: Sampling method

progress.title: A full-correlation subclass is completely classified
progress.detail: Werner and Wolf enumerate all full-correlation facets for arbitrary parties with two dichotomic observables per site, not the full probability polytope for arbitrary scenarios.
progress.label: Restricted classification
